candidates.tagline: The AI loneliness pendant flopped — so they brought it back at double the price
candidates.story: Friend, the AI companionship pendant launched in 2024 at $99 (whose NYC subway ads were immediately graffitied with 'go make some real friends'), relaunched in July 2026 as Friend 2.0 at $249 — now with a speaker — plus a $10/month subscription or it forgets you after 30 days.
candidates.why_funny: The product designed to fix loneliness flopped so hard that the founders' solution was to charge 151% more for it and add a forgetting-you subscription.
candidates.alt: A woman wearing the white circular Friend AI companion pendant around her neck while brushing her teeth, illustrating the always-on AI wearable

candidates.tagline: NYC's new 'protected' bike lane is 4 feet wide. Per direction. On a 34-foot street.
candidates.story: New York City's DOT revealed plans for a two-way 'protected' bike lane on Grand Street in Lower Manhattan that is only 8 feet total — 4 feet per direction — less than half the recommended minimum width, while 23 of the street's 34 feet remain allocated to cars including space for double-parking.
candidates.why_funny: The city's own planning diagram shows cyclists getting a strip barely wider than a car door while the double-parking lane stays, then called it a 'protected' bike path.
candidates.alt: NYC DOT cross-section diagram of Grand Street showing the proposed layout: two car travel lanes and a parking lane taking 23 feet, with only an 8-foot two-way bike lane squeezed into the remainder
candidates.credit: NYC Department of Transportation / Streetsblog NYC
